diffs.diff: acceleration_x_g: datasheet reading gives 3.3333 per count, the part's model has 3.03
diffs.evidence: Both readings use the datasheet's ratiometric law; they differ only in the supply VS. ADXL335 datasheet Rev. 0 Table 1 (VS = 3 V): 'Sensitivity at XOUT, YOUT, ZOUT VS = 3 V 270 300 330 mV/g', '0 g Voltage at XOUT, YOUT VS = 3 V ... 1.5 V'; p.11: 'The ADXL335 output is ratiometric, therefore, the output sensitivity (or scale factor) varies proportionally to the supply voltage. At VS = 3.6 V, the output sensitivity is typically 360 mV/g' and 'the zero g output is nominally equal to VS/2 at all supply voltages.' The second reading's 3.3333 g/V (offset -5) is the bare-chip VS = 3 V test condition (1/0.300 V/g, 0 g at 1.5 V). The modelled product is the GY-61 module, whose VCC pin feeds an on-board 3.3 V regulator (ThaiEasyElec GY-61 Quick Start Guide pin table, pin 1 VCC: 'ขารับไฟ +5 โวลต์ไปที่ Regulate 3.3 โวลต์' = '+5 V supply input to the 3.3 V regulator'), so VS = 3.3 V: 0 g = 1.65 V, 330 mV/g -> 1/0.33 = 3.03 g/V, offset -1.65/0.33 = -5. The model's 3.03 is correct for this product.
